thread.title: Apple Beats December-Quarter Views, Guides Lower For March Quarter

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Beats December-Quarter Views, Guides Lower For March Quarter
text:
Consumer electronics giant Apple ( AAPL ) late Thursday beat Wall Street's targets for revenue and earnings in the December quarter, but came up short on iPhone unit sales, and guided to sales for the March quarter that were well below views.
Apple shares initially fell in after-hours trading on the stock market today , but turned positive when Apple began its conference call with analysts. It was up 2% in extended trading. During the regular session, Apple rose 0.2% to 167.78.
Apple reported earnings per share of $3.89, up 16% year over year, on sales of $88.3 billion, up 13%, for its fiscal first quarter. Analysts expected earnings of $3.82 a share on sales of $86.29 billion for the holiday-sales period, according to Zacks Investment Research.
Apple sold 77.3 million iPhones last quarter, vs. consensus expectations for 80 million. However, because of higher prices for its new models, including the iPhone X and iPhone 8 series handsets, Apple saw a big increase in average selling prices. In the December quarter, Apple's average selling price for iPhones was $796, vs. Street expectations for $756.
For the current quarter, Apple expects sales of $60 billion to $62 billion, missing Wall Street's target of $65.4 billion, according to Zacks. It did not give an earnings-per-share target for its fiscal second quarter, but Wall Street was modeling EPS of $2.79.
Analysts widely expected Apple to guide down for the March quarter, based on evidence of a slowdown in sales of the company's flagship iPhone X smartphone.
Apple's guidance appears to target around 50 million iPhone units in the March quarter, vs. consensus of 59 million, Mizuho Securities analyst Abhey Lamba said in a report to clients.
